pages.text:
MAKE YOUR PLAN TO VOTE
## It's time to take our country back.
Our political system is broken, captured by party bosses, D.C. insiders and corporate donors who install politicians like Kurt Alme to do their bidding. They get rich, while we get higher costs, corruption, endless wars, and data centers in our backyards.
I’m ready to fight for YOU as an Independent in the U.S. Senate.
We’re grateful for your donations!
Your contributions help us reach more voters.
Click an option below to donate online or mail your contribution to
P.O. Box 7188, Missoula, MT 59807.
## Watch Our Campaign Videos
we don't fit in a box
## BOXES
In Washington, they force you into a box: Democrat or Republican. And you vote how you’re told to, even if it hurts your state. I reject that.
## BOUGHT AND PAID FOR
Ever wonder why your gas costs so much? Your prescriptions? Your groceries? You're getting a raw deal because our politicians in D.C. are too busy making themselves rich. They're bought and paid for by the same corporate monopolies that are ripping us off.
## DECLARE YOUR INDEPENDENCE
I've led soldiers in Iraq and through the Philippine jungles as a Green Beret. But now I'm a dad and I'm worried about their future. I'm running for U.S. Senate as an Independent to stand up for Montana. So if you're sick of politics as usual, stop voting for politicians as usual.
## WHY I'M RUNNING
Our country is in crisis. And our national political parties are failing us. Montanans are an independent people, and they deserve an Independent voice for fighting for them in Washington, D.C.
As Montana's Independent Voice in the U.S. Senate, Seth Bodnar will As Montana’s Independent voice in the U.S. Senate, Seth Bodnar will answer only to you, not to party bosses or corporate donors.
Lower costs. Montanans are working harder than ever and falling further behind. Seth will fight to end the war in Iran and the trade wars driving up the cost of fuel, fertilizer, and groceries, restore the health care tax credits that sent premiums soaring, protect the Medicaid expansion that keeps rural hospitals open, and cap insulin at $35 a month for every Montanan. He’ll cut the red tape blocking new housing, stop Wall Street from buying up starter homes, and make sure Big Tech’s data centers never drive up your power bill.
End corruption. A broken political system breeds corruption, and that corruption drives up your costs. Seth will ban stock trading by members of Congress, fight to overturn Citizens United and get dark money out of our elections, and enforce our antitrust laws against the corporate monopolies squeezing Montana ranchers and families.
Defend our freedoms. The government has no place in our doctor’s offices, our bedrooms, or our gun cabinets. Seth will protect our Second Amendment rights, defend a woman’s right to make her own health care decisions, keep our public lands in public hands, and protect Montanans’ privacy from Big Tech.
Seth will work with anyone when it’s good for Montana, and stand up to anyone when it isn’t. Because Montana deserves a senator who puts our state first, every single time.

## EIGHT YEARS OF RESULTS
As President of the University of Montana, Seth Bodnar grew the university into a position of strength. He reversed a decade-long decline and delivered real results for real Montana families. For eight years, he led the state’s flagship top-tier research institution and served over 16,000 students across UM’s affiliated campuses.
During his tenure, he:
Turned around a decade of enrollment decline and grew it to a place of health.
Delivered record-high retention and graduation rates.
Nearly doubled research funding and earned UM's first-ever R1 research status.
Secured UM’s recognition as the #1 university in the nation for community and national service.
Earned UM’s ranking as the #1 military-friendly university in America.
Led the largest fundraising campaign in university history.
Completed the largest campus infrastructure renewal in a generation.
Supported the promotion of women into leadership.
Established wider doors for low-income, first-generation, Native American, and military families.
## ADVANCED WOMEN IN LEADERSHIP AT UM
When Bodnar arrived at the University of Montana:
Zero (0) women held a non-interim vice president title.
Only one (1) woman held a dean position.
During Bodnar's tenure as president at the University of Montana:
The number of women in non-interim vice president positions grew from zero (0) to three (3).
The number of women serving on his senior executive team grew to eight (8), making up half of Bodnar's senior executive team.
Six (6) of these eight (8) senior women leaders were hired during Bodnar's tenure.
The number of women serving as deans grew from one (1) to seven (7) of thirteen (13) deans.
## INVESTED IN SUPPORT OF WOMEN
During Bodnar's tenure as president at the University of Montana:
He relaunched and funded the Women's Leadership Initiative, which had gone dormant prior to his arrival.
He invested and expanded staffing in the Title IX office and promoted an accomplished woman as its leader.
He raised more than $1 million in private dollars for and launched the S.E.A. Change Initiative, which focused on promoting gender equity and which was led by a talented woman leader. Coverage of the efforts noted the work, "should be hailed as an important step toward closing the opportunity and achievement gaps between men and women," and that under Seth's leadership, "UM's acknowledgement of the unique challenges facing women in the workforce and its pledge to help overcome those hurdles therefore holds a lot of promise."
## IN THEIR OWN WORDS: WOMEN'S VOICES
*Titles/affiliation are listed for identification purposes only; all individuals are speaking as private citizens.
## SARAH SWAGER
Former UM Vice Provost for Student Success
"I'm from Sheridan, Montana and worked in higher education for decades. I've seen presidents come and go. Seth was one of the most supportive leaders I have ever worked with. When he arrived, UM had one female dean. When he left, more than half our deans were women. I watched him hire two female provosts, which is the #2 position at the university. He listened to them. I sat at the table and on the executive team, and my voice was always valued. And while I worked to juggle my responsibilities as a leader and my responsibilities as a daughter caring for aging parents, Seth supported me every step of the way."
## ARLENE WALKER-ANDREWS
Former UM Vice Provost for Academic Affairs
"I spent more than 45 years in higher education settings: as a secretary, undergraduate, graduate student, professor, administrator, and volunteer. I recognize the difference between saying you support the people in those positions and actually doing so. In the workplace, women, especially, encounter those who discriminate based on age, gender, race, appearance, and education. Universities are not immune to those forces, which call for leadership that meets that challenge. Seth Bodnar did so. He promoted women across UM; he appointed women to higher administrative positions; and he relaunched the Women's Leadership Initiative to empower women and recognize their contributions. I know personally several of the talented women who were recognized and promoted under his leadership."
## GRACE GARDNER
UM Associate Dean, Missoula College
"I have been part of the University of Montana community since 2005, serving in a variety of roles while earning all four of my degrees from UM. During that time, I completed my doctorate, became a mother of three, and was entrusted with increasing leadership responsibilities, ultimately being promoted to Associate Dean at Missoula College. As a fifth-generation Montanan, I was raised to value hard work, humility, honesty, and authenticity. I've learned to recognize character, and I also know when something doesn't ring true. Based on my own experience, Seth Bodnar has consistently demonstrated integrity, professionalism, kindness, and genuine respect for the people around him. Throughout every stage of my personal and professional journey, Seth was unwavering in his support. He believed in me as a leader, encouraged my growth, and created an environment where I felt trusted and valued. I have worked with many leaders over the course of my career, and he is among the very best. He leads with humility, works incredibly hard, and invests in people. I will always be grateful for the opportunity to have worked under his leadership and for the example he has set for our university community."
## MAGGIE BELL
Former UM Student Body President
"I grew up in Great Falls and met Seth Bodnar when I was a student at the University of Montana serving as the student body president. I learned so much about leadership and taking action just by watching Seth. He listened when I brought ideas or issues forward, took noticeable steps toward solutions, and was willing to put in the work on students' behalf. Seth believed in me as a leader and fostered an environment where I was a welcome and engaged participant — even as the youngest or less experienced person in the room. I refuse to let a political opponent who has never worked with Seth try to further divide Montanans with falsities about who he is. Montana needs Seth in Washington. He will be a true representative of Montanans and our ideas, unique problems, and needs. Being a young woman in leadership is hard but Seth believed in me. And he believes in Montana. I know he won't be in D.C. to serve himself; he'll have all of us in mind, always."
## MARY KRETA
Former UM VP for Enrollment Management
"Seth is one of the most principled and humble leaders I've ever met. At UM, I had the privilege to serve alongside many women I admire. We were hired, promoted, and supported by Seth. As a leader, he mentored us, yes, but he also asked us to teach and mentor him. He respected and empowered each of us in ways that embraced our entire life story and enabled us to reach our full potential. And he recognized that in order to reach his full potential, he needed to humbly listen to us. Seth and I did not always agree, and we regularly debated. He appreciated it when I pushed back or questioned his thinking, especially when a decision had profound consequences. He respected my ideas, trusted my judgement, and deeply considered my perspective when it differed from his."
## RENAE SCOTT
Former UM Chief Information Officer
"I worked closely with Seth Bodnar for a number of years as a member of his executive team. During that time I had his unwavering support both professionally and personally. I always knew his door was open and that I'd find a colleague ready to help me succeed. Characterizations of Seth as anything other than kind, supportive, and ethically oriented do not at all align with what I know to be true of him."
## AMY CAPOLUPO
UM Associate VP and Dean of Students
"I worked with Seth for eight years. What you see, hear, and read from Seth is who he is. He is accountable, fair, and open to feedback. What impresses me most is that he genuinely cares about the people he serves. He approaches leadership as a responsibility and a privilege. He works hard to create opportunities for others while remaining grounded in his principles, and he does not compromise his values simply because it is convenient. He listens carefully, seeks out people with deeper expertise, welcomes candid feedback, and makes thoughtful decisions."
## MARIA MANGOLD
"I worked with Seth Bodnar during his UM presidency and witnessed him lead with emotional intelligence and a willingness to hold himself and others accountable. He demonstrated an ability to take criticism, to repair relationships when needed, and to take responsibility for his own mistakes. I personally witnessed this. He quietly modeled this for all of us. He set a silent yet shared standard of integrity. We deserve this type of leadership in Montana. 'Inclusive prosperity' became both UM's motto and his rallying call."
## GREW ENROLLMENT, STUDENT SUCCESS, AND GRADUATION RATES
Reversed a decade-long enrollment decline, delivering five consecutive years of growth and a record-high first-year retention rate. Improved graduation rates by one-third, achieving an all-time high.
## DROVE RESEARCH & INSTITUTIONAL GROWTH
Grew research award volume by 92% and earned UM's Carnegie R1 research classification, the highest classification for doctoral universities in the United States. This UM classification was reaffirmed in 2025.
## GAINED NATIONAL RECOGNITION
Named the #1 university in the nation for community and national service three years running.
Named the #1 Military Friendly university in the nation among tier-1 research institutions.
## ACHIEVED FUNDRAISING RECORDS
Completed the largest fundraising campaign in state history — $450.9 million from more than 34,000 donors — and grew the university's endowment by more than 60%.
## GREW WORKFORCE & ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
Launched AccelerateMT, training more than 3,300 Montanans through non-credit, short-term programs that saw a completion and job-placement rate above 90%.
## ADVANCED CYBERSECURITY & TECHNOLOGY LEADERSHIP
Secured $6 million to launch CyberMontana and establish the state's first four-year cybersecurity degree program.
## INVESTED IN INFRASTRUCTURE & CAMPUS RENEWAL
Spearheaded a $400 million campus infrastructure renewal, the largest in university history, investing in student living and learning spaces, in community spaces, and in core facilities to serve future generations of Montanans.
## ACHIEVED FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY
Eliminated a $10 million structural budget deficit and improved the university's net asset position by nearly $60 million.
Built new revenue streams through efforts like summer concerts in the football stadium, bringing economic benefit not just to the university but also to the local economy.
## IMPROVED ORGANIZATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS
Overhauled strategic planning and built an integrated HR function to strengthen recruiting and retention.
## DROVE ATHLETIC SUCCESS
Delivered major athletic facility upgrades — including the state's first indoor practice facility — and led Grizzly football to its first national championship game since 2009.
## IMPROVED INSTITUTIONAL BRANDING
Oversaw a major institutional branding refresh that authentically captured UM’s identity and injected new energy into UM’s public face.
## PROVIDED STEADY LEADERSHIP
Guided the university through a global pandemic, emerging stronger on the other side.
## SETH'S LEADERSHIP FOCUS AT UM: INCLUSIVE PROSPERITY FOR ALL MONTANANS
Bondar’s efforts to drive progress at the University of Montana were all in the service of a larger goal as president: to promote inclusive prosperity for all Montanans through opportunities for all to reach their full, unique potential. This is demonstrated in his success expanding the university's graduate school, dual-enrollment programs, and workforce training initiatives. These efforts aimed to ensure every Montanan would have access to the education and training needed to secure a well-paying job and meaningful career.
Bodnar prioritized several efforts to support this goal, including:
Native American Students — UM recorded the largest number of Native American students in the university's history and increased enrollment of Native American students by more than 40% from 2018.
Veterans and Military-Connected Students — UM was ranked the #1 "Military Friendly" college in the country among tier-1 research institutions in 2025, serving roughly 1,000 military-affiliated students.
First-Generation College Students — Under Bodnar's leadership, first-generation students grew to 33% of the student body by fall 2025.
Workforce Training — Under Bodnar's leadership, short-term workforce training was a priority. UM served 10,387 individuals through noncredit workforce training programs during the 2024-25 school year alone.
